findings: Bun Promise-truth law (NEW, fleet TS code): Bun.spawn's proc.exited is a Promise<number> — ALWAYS truthy — so 'if (!child || child.exited)' spawns a fresh child per call (measured: 7 spawns for 7 calls, each paying the full 1.8s cold path). Law: liveness is an explicit flag set in the exited handler; never truth-test a Promise. Fixed live; amortization receipt (7.5-8.6ms) only exists because of the fix.

amortization ladder end-to-end (extends CR-0029): one-shot CLI 5.5s -> daemon CLI 2.0s -> raw stdio session 12-15ms -> GOVERNED HTTP HOST 7.5-8.6ms warm (1.8s cold paid once per child). The most governed surface is also the fastest — policy costs nothing at the warm floor.

stream hygiene law (NEW): stdout and stderr of the engine child each get their OWN line buffer (a shared buffer interleaves engine stderr into JSON-RPC responses and corrupts them) and stderr MUST be drained (an undrained pipe can deadlock the child mid-response). Both found during this rung; fixed before the receipt battery.

double-enforcement composition (NEW, booked): belt (host allowlist) fires before braces (engine --tool-profile) — the engine never sees denied calls, which both saves engine work and keeps the engine's own logs free of policy noise; profiles stay faithful copies of the engine registry so belt and braces can never disagree about the analysis surface.
